main_body: A wooden loom frame drawn straight from the front. Brown wooden border, a cream warp-thread panel with vertical stripes, a red and yellow checkered woven band, and two short legs below.
top_band: Rows 10-12 are brown/tan wood (#b77246, #d59147), about 3 rows. It reads as the frame's front crossbeam rather than a horizontal surface, and is no lighter than the lower beam at rows 22-23, which has the same tones. Nothing is separated from the front face by a step.
evidence: The top beam (rows 10-12) has the same tones as the bottom beam (rows 22-23), so it is a vertical face of the frame and not a top surface. The warp threads, the weaving band and the side posts are all painted flat on one front plane, like an architectural elevation. No beam top, base top or other horizontal surface is visible from above. The legs below are plain vertical strips. This matches the guide's red 'front elevation' example.

style.evidence: The outline is a dark brown tinted to the wood, and the 0% neutral share confirms it is tinted. Colours per tile (11) are lower than the references (17 and 20), and only 12 distinct colours against 38-40. The cream warp threads and the red/yellow checker band add some texture, with no 5x5 flat fill. The wood beams have only 3-4 steps, with little grain or per-plank variation. This is clearly thinner than the references' 5-6 step ramps and their rich detail, so it is not equal to the reference.
